description: Uh oh. The joists above sit right on top of this wall. It's holding up the second floor.
option_1: Knock it out and add a few 2x4s later
option_2: Rebuild the entire second-floor framing
option_3: Hire an engineer to design a beam

description: The new post lands on a slab that's barely 4 inches thick. That's not a footing, that's a sidewalk.
option_1: Set the post on a stack of pavers
option_2: Replace the whole foundation
option_3: Pour a new footing under the post

description: Surprise! Three circuits run through this wall, including the one for the fridge.
option_1: Have an electrician reroute the circuits
option_2: Tape the wire ends and leave them hanging
option_3: Rewire the whole house

description: The electrician frowns at your panel. It's full, and it might be older than you.
option_1: Double up wires on one breaker
option_2: Go solar with battery backup
option_3: Upgrade the electrical panel

description: Bad news. A big vent pipe runs right up the middle of the wall.
option_1: Box it into a decorative column
option_2: Redo all the upstairs bathroom plumbing
option_3: Reroute the vent to a nearby wall

description: The test kit is back. The old joint compound has asbestos. Fun!
option_1: Hire a licensed abatement crew
option_2: Sell the house
option_3: Wear a dust mask and keep swinging

description: With the wall gone, oak meets laminate in a very straight, very obvious line.
option_1: Cover the seam with a big rug
option_2: Replace the floors in both rooms
option_3: Install a transition strip

description: Your ceiling patch is smooth. The rest of the ceiling is popcorn. Everyone will notice.
option_1: Spray matching texture on the patch
option_2: Scrape and retexture the whole ceiling
option_3: Leave it, nobody looks up

description: Standing in the new open space, you suddenly need a kitchen island. Need.
option_1: Build an island with a sink this month
option_2: Sketch it for next year
option_3: Push the dining table over and call it an island

description: Your partner: "Since the tools are out, the bedroom door is squeaking again."
option_1: Replace every door in the house
option_2: Take the door off and leave it in the garage
option_3: Lube the hinge after cleanup

description: The engineer's beam is deeper than your ceiling joists. It's not going to hide up there.
option_1: Use a dropped beam below the ceiling
option_2: Notch the beam so it fits
option_3: Raise the second floor

description: There's an HVAC duct inside the wall feeding the upstairs bedroom. It was not on the plans.
option_1: Replace the whole HVAC system
option_2: Reroute the duct through the ceiling
option_3: Cut the duct and cap both ends

description: The new vent path runs straight into a floor joist. Naturally.
option_1: Cut through the joist
option_2: Route around the joist with fittings
option_3: Move the upstairs bathroom

description: The abatement crew can't come for three weeks, and the wall is half open.
option_1: Clean it up yourself with a shop vac
option_2: Seal off the area with plastic and wait
option_3: Pay triple for a rush crew

description: Where the wall stood, a 5-inch strip of bare subfloor stares back at you.
option_1: Fill it with wood filler
option_2: Replace the floors in both rooms
option_3: Weave in boards salvaged from a closet

description: You finally find your exact flooring online. Discontinued in 2014.
option_1: Patch with a close-enough board
option_2: Refloor the entire house
option_3: Hunt for leftover boxes on resale sites

description: The top plate is gone, leaving a long, ragged slot across the ceiling.
option_1: Cover it with a strip of trim
option_2: Add blocking and patch with drywall
option_3: Leave it open as a design feature

description: You sent a popcorn sample to the lab just in case. It came back with asbestos.
option_1: Have it abated before any scraping
option_2: Drywall over every ceiling in the house
option_3: Scrape it wet and hope for the best

description: The ceiling is already patched. What if... can lights. Everywhere.
option_1: Run extension cords across the ceiling
option_2: Plan them for a future project
option_3: Cut in twelve can lights tonight

description: The fresh open room makes the hallway look gray and gloomy.
option_1: Hang more art to distract from it
option_2: Touch up the worst scuffs
option_3: Repaint the whole house
